chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bashshar (may God have mercy on him) narrated that Abul Faraj al-Mudhaffar ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan al-Qazvini narrated that Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qasim ibn Hamza ibn Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated that Al-Hasan ibn Sahl al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) about the exaggerators and those who believe in God turning over the affairs, so he said:

The exaggerators are disbelievers and those who believe in (God) turning over the affairs are polytheists. Whoever sits with them, mixes with them, eats with them, drinks with them, becomes related to them, gives a daughter in marriage to them or marries one of their daughters, grants them immunity, considers them honest in keeping what they are entrusted with, or acknowledges what they say or assists them with half a word, has exited from the guardianship of God, the Exalted and Mighty, and the guardianship of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and our guardianship, the People of the House.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْغُلَاةُ: The exaggerators, a sect known for attributing divine qualities to Imams
key_terms.وَالْمُفَوِّضَةُ: Those who believe in divine delegation of all affairs to a specific figure

ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for exiting the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt according to Imam Ar-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Rida (AS) distinguishes the Ghulat, who exaggerate in the divinity of the Imams, as disbelievers, from the Mufawidha, who attribute divine agency to the Prophet, as polytheists. He establishes a rigorous standard of social intimacy—such as dining, marrying, or entrusting secrets—whereby mere association with these groups results in the loss of Wilayah, emphasizing that theological deviation corrupts communal bonds. This narration underscores the Shia principle that correct belief is intrinsically linked to social conduct and loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 46-4 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Bashshar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abul Faraj al-Mudhaffar ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Hassan al-Qazvini quoted on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qasim ibn Hamza ibn Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s.), on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Sahl al-Qummi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abi Hashem al-Ja’fari that he had asked Abal Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) about the exaggerators and those who believed in (God) turning over (all) the affairs. The Imam (a.s.) replied, “

The exaggerators are unbelievers and those who believe in (God) turning over (all) the affairs (to the Prophet (sw)) are polytheists. Whoever associates with them; visits them; eats or drinks with them; becomes related to them; gives a daughter in marriage to or marries with one of their daughters; grants them immunity; considers them honest in keeping what they are entrusted with; or acknowledges what they say or assists them in what they say has exited from the circle of the Mastery of the Honorable the Exalted God, the Mastery of the Messenger (sw) and the Mastery of us - the Members of the Holy Household.”
